passages.original: Quod gratia Dei non solum peccata dimittat, sed etiam adjuvet ne committantur, et praestet ut lex impleatur; non sicut ait Pelagius, facite, quasi sine gratia Dei difficilius possit impleri.
passages.english: That the grace of God not only forgives sins, but also helps [us] so that they are not committed, and grants that the law be fulfilled; not, as Pelagius says, "easily," as if without the grace of God it could [only] be fulfilled with greater difficulty.
passages.notes: This is a chapter heading. The Latin "facite" ("do") is abrupt and may be corrupt or abbreviated; the Pelagian position usually cited is that grace is given so that what is commanded may be fulfilled more easily (facilius), as if it could be done without grace, though with more difficulty. "Facite" may be a misreading of an original such as "facilius".
